findings.title: Alleged 'double charge' on 2026-09-14 is not a duplicate — it's an authorization + settlement pair
findings.explanation: TX-9002 was a $149 authorization (temporary hold) that hit a gateway capture timeout and was never captured; it was released on 2026-09-18 with no funds taken. TX-9001 is the actual settlement for INV-2609, captured and settled 2026-09-15. Per POL-B-AUTH, a released authorization is not a charge and is not refundable — no double charge occurred. SUP-5601's agent conclusion of 'duplicate charge' and the resulting promise to refund $149 within 5-7 business days was made without billing review and is itself an error under POL-B-REF, which requires billing-specialist approval before any refund is promised. SUP-5602 correctly escalated/paused this before acting.

findings.title: Deep Time Analytics $30 add-on charge is legitimate
findings.explanation: The add-on was added 2026-09-12 by U-2, an admin seat, which is permitted under POL-B-ADD (owner or any admin may add add-ons). It started at the next renewal (2026-09-14) and was invoiced separately at full monthly price ($30), exactly as policy dictates. No billing error.

findings.title: July upgrade charge ($59.60) is correct proration; prior support answer was incomplete
findings.explanation: INV-2607P's $59.60 charge matches POL-B-PRO's formula (new plan price x remaining_days/period_days for the upgrade). SUP-5549's conclusion 'no credit due' was correct as to the invoice itself (no invoice-line credit belongs there), but incomplete: proration policy independently generates an account credit for unused time on the old plan, and that credit (CR-778, $19.60) was in fact issued the same day. The charge itself was not an error, but the customer was not told about the separately-issued credit.

findings.title: Unapplied CR-778 credit never flagged to owner — policy violation
findings.explanation: Auto-apply-credits was disabled 2026-05-02 per customer request (SUP-5390), with the commitment that credits remain on the account until the customer requests application. CR-778 ($19.60) was issued 2026-07-02 and remains unapplied with owner_notified=false. It is now well over 30 days old. POL-B-CRD requires that with auto-apply disabled, unapplied credits older than 30 days must be flagged to the account owner (owner_notified=true) and then applied or refunded per the owner's instruction. This notification never happened — an actual, unresolved billing-process error independent of the disputed charges.

findings.title: CR-512 goodwill credit correctly applied
findings.explanation: The $5 goodwill credit from SUP-5201 was applied to INV-2602 as recorded. No discrepancy found.

corrections.prior_claim: Agent concluded the customer was charged twice on 2026-09-14 (duplicate charge) and promised a $149 refund within 5-7 business days.
corrections.corrected_claim: There was no duplicate charge. TX-9002 was an uncaptured authorization released after a gateway capture timeout; only TX-9001 settled for $149 against INV-2609. Per POL-B-AUTH a released, uncaptured authorization is not refundable because no funds were taken. The refund promise was also made without billing-specialist review, violating POL-B-REF.

corrections.prior_claim: Agent concluded 'no credit due' regarding the July upgrade charge.
corrections.corrected_claim: The upgrade charge itself was correctly prorated and no credit belongs on that invoice, but this answer omitted that a separate account credit (CR-778, $19.60) for unused old-plan time was issued the same day per POL-B-PRO — that credit still exists, unapplied, and was never disclosed to the customer.

unresolved_questions: Should CR-778 ($19.60) be applied to a future invoice or refunded — pending the account owner's instruction once properly notified, per POL-B-CRD.
Whether SUP-5601's improper refund promise needs to be formally retracted/communicated to the customer by an authorized support agent (this agent cannot contact the customer).
Whether any process/training follow-up is warranted for the SUP-5601 agent who promised a refund without billing review, contrary to POL-B-REF.

actions_requiring_human_authorization.description: Notify the account owner (per POL-B-CRD) that credit CR-778 ($19.60, issued 2026-07-02) remains unapplied, and ask for instruction to apply it to an invoice or refund it.
Formally withdraw/correct the $149 refund promise made in SUP-5601, since it was based on a misdiagnosis (no actual duplicate charge occurred) and was made without required billing-specialist review.
Apply CR-778 to an invoice, or issue a refund of $19.60, once the account owner has been notified and gives instruction, per POL-B-CRD.

Communicate final resolution to customer on all three disputed items (no double charge, add-on charge is legitimate, July proration correct but a $19.60 credit is available) and correct the earlier incorrect refund promise.
